articles.title: Crypto.com to Shut Hong Kong App in February
articles.text:
Crypto.com to withdraw Hong Kong consumer app citing regulatory changes
Crypto.com will discontinue its consumer app services in Hong Kong in February next year.
Update (Nov. 3, 2026, 11:10 am UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from a Crypto.com spokesperson.
Crypto.com will discontinue its consumer app services in Hong Kong on Feb. 1, 2027, while continuing to pursue regulatory approval for its institutional exchange.
On Tuesday, a Crypto.com spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company would discontinue its consumer app services in Hong Kong. The spokesperson said all affected customers had received advance notice and would receive instructions on closing their accounts and support to withdraw their funds.
According to local news outlet HK01, Crypto.com cited regulatory changes in emails sent to its users in Hong Kong. The consumer app is operated by Foris DAX MT Limited, while a separate entity, Foris DAX HK Limited, is seeking a Hong Kong virtual asset trading platform license.
According to the Securities and Futures Commission’s (SFC) public register, the company’s Hong Kong entity submitted its VATP license application on Feb. 9, 2024. Nearly three years later, Foris DAX HK Limited remains listed as “deemed-to-be-licensed” — a transitional status rather than full regulatory approval.
The spokesperson said the shutdown reflects Crypto.com’s efforts to optimize global operations and allocate resources toward sustainable long-term opportunities. However, the statement did not specify which regulatory changes prompted the decision.
Crypto.com also plans to continue pursuing the VATP license application for its institutional platform. The company said it remains committed to the broader Asia-Pacific region and working with regulators worldwide to support responsible industry growth.
Related: Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

articles.title: Coinbase XRP looked cheap on Nov. 2 despite identical market value
articles.text:
Quick Take
- XRP’s Nov. 2 Coinbase discount shrank from 0.168% to 0.006% after converting Binance’s USDT quote into dollars.
- Seven completed daily observations retained residual discounts on Oct. 30 and 31, limiting any universal parity conclusion.
- A separate 60-minute sample shifted to a small adjusted premium, while comparable seller-initiated flow remains unestablished.
XRP’s apparent Coinbase discount at the Nov. 2 close shrinks from about 0.168% to 0.006% when Binance’s Tether (USDT) quote is converted into dollars. The independent exchange-price comparison separates the quote-currency effect from the remaining difference in XRP prices.
The user Arab Chain on CryptoQuant reported an approximately -0.16% XRP Coinbase Premium Index reading on Nov. 2, describing it as an eight-month low and interpreting it as relatively weaker Coinbase demand.
The post also cautioned that the index alone was not definitive evidence of continued downside pressure.
What the dollar conversion changes
The completed Nov. 2 candles put Coinbase XRP/USD at $1.2481, Binance XRP/USDT at 1.2502 USDT and Coinbase USDT/USD at $0.99838.
The adjustment multiplies Binance’s XRP price by USDT’s dollar price, then compares Coinbase against that converted figure. Expressed as a percentage, the formula is:
100 × [Coinbase XRP/USD ÷ (Binance XRP/USDT × USDT/USD) − 1].
This uses Coinbase’s USDT/USD market as the conversion reference. It is a venue price, rather than a universal redemption rate or evidence about why USDT traded below one dollar.
Across all seven completed UTC daily observations, the adjustment narrowed the discount, but did not eliminate it every day:
| UTC date (2026) | Raw gap | Dollar-adjusted gap | 
|---|---|---|
| Oct. 27 | -0.135% | -0.001% | 
| Oct. 28 | -0.128% | -0.019% | 
| Oct. 29 | -0.226% | -0.002% | 
| Oct. 30 | -0.199% | -0.066% | 
| Oct. 31 | -0.200% | -0.078% | 
| Nov. 1 | -0.128% | +0.002% | 
| Nov. 2 | -0.168% | -0.006% | 
Negative values mean Coinbase was cheaper, while positive values mean it was more expensive. Figures are rounded to three decimal places from the three exchange datasets.
Oct. 30 and 31 adjusted discounts remained about 0.066% and 0.078%, respectively, and the Nov. 2 finding supports checking the currency conversion.
A separate check used 60 matched one-minute buckets from Nov. 2, 12:00-12:59 UTC, combining Coinbase XRP/USD, Binance XRP/USDT and Coinbase USDT/USD. Its median raw gap was about -0.128%, and the median dollar-adjusted gap was approximately +0.006%.
XRP was near $1.28 on Nov. 3. Around 13:15 UTC, Coinbase’s ticker reported a $1.276 last trade, above its $1.2481 Nov. 2 close, while Binance’s rolling ticker showed 1.2780 USDT.
What would establish weaker XRP demand?
A relative-demand warning would be more persuasive if a discount persisted after currency conversion alongside comparatively heavier seller-initiated XRP trading over equivalent windows.
The measurement stops short of an executable arbitrage test. Coinbase defines candle closes as the last trade within each bucket, while Binance’s candles use matching time intervals. Rounding, bid-ask spreads, fees, and differences between venues are important when a residual gap is this small.
An August 2025 XRP liquidity study exposed a similar disconnect: XRP prices remained closely aligned across Binance and Coinbase even as trading activity was concentrated in different quote currencies.
Price consistency does not guarantee equally accessible liquidity, and traders may see nearly identical quotes but face substantially different execution costs and slippage, particularly during periods of market stress.
On Nov. 2’s closing observations, the unadjusted gap by itself substantially overstates the remaining dollar-price difference.

articles.title: Australia Hikes Rates to 18-Year High as AI Fuels Inflation
articles.text:
Australia lifts rates to 18-year high as AI boom, energy costs fuel inflation
The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its benchmark rate to 4.85% on rising technology costs from AI investment and higher energy prices.
Australia’s central bank raised its interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Tuesday, warning that inflation would stay elevated through much of 2027 as energy costs and AI-related investment added to price pressures.
The Reserve Bank of Australia’s monetary policy board voted 6–3 for the increase, with three members preferring to hold rates at 4.60%.
The bank pushed back its forecast for inflation to return to the top of its 2% to 3% target range until late 2027, around three quarters later than previously expected.
“AI-related investment is driving rapid growth in prices for technology-related goods,” the board said, alongside higher fuel and commodity prices affected by the Middle East conflict. The interest rate in Australia is now at its highest level in 18 years.
“Today’s decision by the RBA was widely expected, but that doesn’t make it any easier for families and businesses,” said Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers. “It’s difficult news for many Australians who are already paying a hefty price for circumstances outside their control.”
The increase contrasts with the US Federal Reserve’s decision to hold rates last week, even as Fed officials have also warned that the AI investment boom is adding to price pressures, including for computer equipment and utilities.
Related: Fed’s hawkish rate hold keeps pressure on Bitcoin: Analysts

articles.title: Binance relied on AI to fight fraud before hackers exploited internal tool in $6 billion theft
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Hackers exploited Binance's internal AI tool to compromise wallet engineers before stealing $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency.
- The breach exposed security weaknesses at an exchange that relied on more than 100 AI models.
- Binance is seeking partnerships with leading AI firms and commissioning an independent security review, with key details of both initiatives undisclosed.
Hackers exploited Binance's internal artificial intelligence tools to compromise engineers before stealing $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency, the exchange disclosed.
In its Nov. 3 security report, Binance said attackers used a compromised employee computer and an internal AI tool on Oct. 20 to take control of two engineers responsible for its wallet infrastructure.
The attackers subsequently obtained access to a container deployment permission token, which helped them penetrate the exchange's wallet-signing operations on Oct. 29 and initiate unauthorized transactions across several blockchain networks.
The disclosure puts AI at the center of one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record, adding to concerns about how increasingly connected AI systems can introduce new vulnerabilities into corporate infrastructure.
Binance's investigation does not establish that an AI model autonomously planned or executed the theft. Rather, the attackers exploited an internal AI tool as part of a broader campaign involving stolen credentials, compromised developer software, and social engineering.
In June, a Binance engineer downloaded a tampered software installer while attempting to install a popular AI coding tool. Binance detected the suspicious activity, replaced the device and rotated associated credentials, although information about the employee and colleagues had already been exposed.
In September, another engineer fell victim to a fake recruitment operation involving staged job interviews and a malicious coding assignment. The malware compromised the employee's computer and gave the attackers access, which they later used to move deeper into Binance's systems.
The FBI has attributed the broader attack to North Korea, whose hacking operations have increasingly targeted software developers and cryptocurrency businesses.
AI becomes a growing weapon in cyberattacks
The Binance incident follows months of warnings from cybersecurity researchers that artificial intelligence is expanding both hackers' capabilities and the systems available for exploitation.
In February, Google's Mandiant reported that North Korean hackers targeting the cryptocurrency industry had incorporated AI-assisted techniques into their operations.
The researchers documented an intrusion involving a fake video conference, malicious software, and a suspected AI-generated video impersonating a corporate executive. They could not independently confirm the deepfake in that particular incident but identified the group's use of AI tools for reconnaissance and social engineering.
By September, Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that attackers were moving beyond using AI to generate malicious content toward automated operations that could execute multiple stages of an intrusion.
In one case, hackers compromised a cloud resource and organized an AI-assisted mass credential-harvesting campaign in less than six hours. Google also identified attackers attempting to manipulate AI coding assistants and security scanners during software supply-chain compromises.
The findings closely resemble one aspect of the Binance breach: developers and the AI-powered tools they depend on are becoming targets attackers use to reach sensitive systems.
Separately, AI developer Anthropic disclosed in September that criminals and suspected state-sponsored operators had used its Claude models to conduct reconnaissance, develop exploitation tools, and automate data theft.
Some operations involved AI agents carrying out multiple stages of an attack with limited human supervision, reducing the technical expertise and manpower traditionally required.
Binance turns to AI companies to strengthen security
The exchange is now seeking support from the same industry whose technologies were featured in the attack.
Binance said it is working to establish a security research fund and develop targeted initiatives with leading AI companies, blockchain industry participants and cybersecurity firms.
The proposed collaboration will focus on strengthening AI security in blockchain environments, although the exchange has not disclosed the fund's proposed size, participating companies or launch date.
It also plans to expand spending on AI-enabled threat detection, endpoint protection, developer-environment security and behavioral anomaly monitoring.
The exchange said it has already rebuilt the affected internal AI tool and wallet infrastructure, replaced compromised employee devices and strengthened access controls.
Binance has also commissioned an independent cybersecurity review to validate its investigation and identify additional safeguards.
The company said approximately $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion in affected digital assets has been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of Oct. 31.
The independent review has yet to establish the full extent of the weaknesses that allowed attackers to exploit the exchange's internal AI environment. Its findings will inform the security changes Binance plans to implement as it develops the proposed industry fund.

articles.title: UK Warns AI Ransomware Attack on Infrastructure by 2028
articles.text:
UK warns AI ransomware attack on infrastructure ‘highly likely’ by 2028
The warning comes as UK cyber officials also flag growing threats from state-backed hackers targeting government officials and politicians.
AI-powered malware is highly likely to be used in a ransomware attack targeting UK critical national infrastructure by 2028, the country’s National Cyber Security Centre has warned.
The assessment, published in the NCSC’s Annual Review 2026, says artificial intelligence will increase the scale and efficiency of ransomware operations, social engineering and vulnerability exploitation.
“It is also highly likely that between now and 2028, AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI,” the report states.
The warning forms part of a broader assessment linking cyber threats to the UK’s economic and national security. The NCSC also warned China, Russia and other nation-states will use “AI cyber” to achieve their geopolitical goals, increasing the scale and speed of cyber threats facing the UK.
Beyond ransomware, the NCSC highlighted the growing threat of state-backed cyber espionage targeting politicians, government officials and other high-risk individuals.
During the year, the NCSC observed persistent spear‑phishing activity against high‑risk individuals and increasing efforts to compromise messaging applications.
In March, Dutch intelligence agencies warned that Russian state hackers were targeting officials, military personnel and civil servants worldwide. Attackers impersonated Signal support to hijack accounts.
“Technology has always influenced cyber security. What is different today is the pace. The ability of state actors to harness new technologies will increasingly determine their effectiveness,” said the NCSC.
Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says

articles.title: Bitcoin investors could pay the price as the Federal Reserve tightens bank lending rules
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Domestic banks reported tighter standards across all five nonbank borrower categories in the Fed's Nov. 2 survey.
- Business-lender standards showed 22% of net tightening, while most responding banks left approvals unchanged.
- Wider credit spreads signal financing pressure, while an older broad index tempers claims of a systemic squeeze reaching Bitcoin.
Banks tightened loan approval standards for nonbank financial firms while reporting stronger demand from business lenders and private-equity funds, according to the Federal Reserve's Nov. 2 lending survey.
That combination points to a financing constraint that could limit investors' appetite for Bitcoin beyond changes in the Fed's policy rate.
For business lenders, classified as business credit intermediaries in the survey, 12 of 50 responding domestic banks tightened standards, one eased, and 37 left them unchanged. The response table shows 24% tightening versus 2% easing, for a net tightening of 22%.
The October Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey covers the preceding three months, generally the third quarter. Responses were due Oct. 5, well before the late-October spread widening.
Domestic banks reported net tightening across all five nonbank borrower categories surveyed. They most often cited a less favorable or more uncertain economic outlook and deterioration in borrowers' financial strength.
At the same time, banks reported stronger demand from business credit intermediaries and private-equity funds in a question measuring funds actually disbursed.
Among banks reporting stronger nonbank demand, common reasons included working-capital or liquidity needs, refinancing, and financial investment opportunities. Banks can become more selective even as borrowers seek financing for both cash needs and investments.
Tighter approvals. Different clocks.
A minority of banks tightened business-lender standards, producing a 22-point net balance. The survey and market indicators describe different periods.
Approval tightening is real, but neither its bank-share measure nor these mismatched dates establishes Bitcoin selling.
- The Federal Reserve's October SLOOS, released November 2, reports that domestic banks tightened standards on net across all five queried nonbank financial borrower categories during the prior quarter, generally Q3 2026. Fed SLOOS November 2 release
- For business credit intermediaries, 12 of 50 responding domestic banks tightened standards, one eased and 37 left them unchanged: 24% minus 2% yields net tightening of 22 percentage points. Fed SLOOS domestic-bank Table 1 Fed SLOOS domestic-bank Table 1
- The survey was sent September 21 and responses were due October 5; 61 domestic banks and 18 US branches and agencies of foreign banks responded. Fed SLOOS November 2 release
- The ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread available on FRED rose from 3.14% on October 28 to 3.44% on October 30, a 30-basis-point widening; October 30 was the latest observation in the November 3 morning retrieval. ICE high-yield spread via FRED
- The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index stood at -0.487 for the week ending October 23, the latest observation available in the November 3 morning retrieval; negative readings indicate conditions looser than average. Chicago Fed NFCI via FRED
Survey covers Q3, with responses due Oct. 5. NFCI describes the week ending Oct. 23; spreads compare Oct. 28 and 30, the latest data exposed Nov. 3 morning. These separate measures do not establish Bitcoin selling.
Method: One square represents one of 50 banks answering Q29B: 12 tightened, 37 unchanged, 1 eased. Verified arithmetic: 12/50=24%, 1/50=2%, and (12−1)/50=22 percentage points net. Spread change: (3.44−3.14)×100=30 basis points. Date positions are schematic, not a time-proportional or causal scale.
How tighter credit could reach Bitcoin
Approval standards determine access to credit, so financing can become harder to obtain without a new policy-rate increase. The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, a separate decision from the earlier lending conditions captured by the survey.
If financing becomes harder to secure while liquidity needs rise, investors may have less capacity or willingness to hold risky assets. A 2023 IMF working paper found that US monetary tightening historically reduced a common crypto-price factor through that channel.
The ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread rose from 3.14% on Oct. 28 to 3.44% on Oct. 30, a widening of 30 basis points.
The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index was -0.487 for the week ending Oct. 23, indicating conditions looser than average.
A stronger signal of spillover would be continued widening in credit premiums alongside weakening Bitcoin demand, while narrowing spreads and resilient demand would weaken that case. For now, the survey shows a financing constraint worth watching.

articles.title: Binance Starts Second Withdrawal Phase After $6.3B Hack
articles.text:
Binance begins second withdrawal phase, exchange outflows slow
The exchange says additional assets will become available for withdrawal from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday as security checks are completed, following an initial reopening on Sunday.
Binance plans to begin a second phase of cryptocurrency withdrawals on Tuesday, as data shows withdrawal volumes have started to stabilize following last week’s $6.3 billion hack.
Withdrawals for additional assets are scheduled to resume progressively from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday, according to Binance’s latest recovery notice. The rollout follows an initial reopening on Nov. 1.
“Like phase one, reopening will roll out progressively across the assets as security and readiness checks are completed,” said Binance.
The exchange said it was prioritizing tokens based on user demand over the past week. Deposits remain available.
Networks part of the second phase of withdrawals include Binance Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base, according to Binance.
Binance’s list of assets planned for withdrawal. Source: Binance
On Monday, Binance said it also reopened withdrawals for several fiat currencies, including the US dollar, United Arab Emirates dirham, Vietnamese dong, Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah, adding to a list of 23 other currencies already available for withdrawal.
Binance exchange outflows slow
Data from DefiLlama shows outflows from the crypto exchange have slowed since Sunday, with net outflows on Monday at $2.57 billion, compared to $6.1 billion the day before.
In a separate security reminder, Binance warned that scammers could exploit the phased reopening by impersonating the exchange and offering accelerated withdrawals, sell priority processing, help users claim compensation or direct them to move assets into a purported “Binance vault,” the exchange said.
“Anyone promising to expedite it for a fee is scamming you,” Binance said.
Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack

articles.title: Binance says thinly traded tokens are delaying full replacement of stolen assets
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance's November 3 plan calls for withdrawals to reopen progressively as each asset-network pair clears security checks.
- The 95% replenishment figure was reported November 1 and repeated November 2; remaining tokens are harder to source.
- Binance says its completed reserve proof covers ten tokens at an Oct. 31 snapshot; a broader snapshot is planned for Nov. 4.
Binance said in its Nov. 2 recovery update that less-liquid tokens were slowing the replacement of stolen assets. It put the outstanding replenishment at approximately 5% of the impacted amount, while a separate withdrawal phase was scheduled for Nov. 3.
The new phase was scheduled to begin at 04:00 UTC. In Binance's Nov. 3 update, the exchange said availability would expand progressively as security and readiness checks were completed for individual assets and networks.
Together, the disclosures explain why a commitment to cover stolen funds can coexist with unfinished recovery. Funding the purchases, obtaining the specific tokens and restoring the routes through which customers withdraw them are separate tasks.
Why the remaining tokens take longer
Binance reported approximately 95% replenishment of the impacted amount in its Nov. 1 recovery update. It repeated that figure on Nov. 2, attributing the outstanding portion to tokens outside the ten assets it said were fully backed: BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC.
The exchange said the remaining assets were less liquid and took longer to source in the required quantities. It described continued purchases through market and over-the-counter channels, alongside work with industry partners to finish the acquisitions.
In its Oct. 31 update, Binance identified corporate treasury, a planned partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users and a portion of its futures insurance resources as recovery funding sources.
The percentage also has a narrower meaning than a general recovery score. Binance describes the denominator as the impacted amount. It does not specify the valuation basis in those disclosures, so the remaining 5% cannot safely be converted into a dollar shortfall. Nor does 95% describe the proportion of tokens or withdrawal routes restored.
Binance's Nov. 2 update said the zero-knowledge proof for its Oct. 31, 00:00 UTC reserve snapshot was complete. It said holders of the ten named tokens could independently verify that their balances were backed at least one-for-one.
The proof concerns a defined set of assets at a dated snapshot. Backing at that snapshot does not establish present availability of every withdrawal route.
The latest withdrawal table illustrates why the network matters alongside the token. It includes RLUSD on Ethereum and XRP, and USDC on Sui, among routes planned for progressive reopening. Those entries identify the scope of the rollout, not which tokens remain unreplenished or whether each route is currently operational.
Restoring each withdrawal route
Binance said it was prioritizing tokens according to demand over the preceding week and restoring each network-asset pair after security checks.
For holders, the immediate check is the chosen asset and network. Binance directed users to its withdrawal page or network-status page to confirm availability, and warned that rollout traffic could cause temporary delays or longer processing times.
A separate transparency milestone is still ahead. Binance said it planned a Nov. 4 reserve snapshot covering more tokens, followed by proof generation estimated to take approximately 40 to 50 hours.
Binance reiterated that it would bear the financial impact of the stolen funds rather than pass losses on to users.

articles.title: South Korea Urges More Cold Storage After Binance Hack
articles.text:
South Korea urges exchanges to boost cold storage after Binance hack
South Korean crypto exchanges are already required to hold at least 80% of customer crypto in cold wallets, but the regulator is urging more.
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has urged domestic crypto exchanges to increase the proportion of assets held in cold wallets after the $6.3 billion attack on Binance last week.
In a statement Monday, the FSC said it held an emergency meeting with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA) and major crypto service providers to review the impact of the Binance hack on South Korea’s crypto market and review exchanges’ security measures.
The FSC said it reviewed exchanges’ IT access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privileges. It also urged providers to increase the proportion of assets held in offline cold wallets.
Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance’s internet-connected hot wallets last week, moving most of the funds in about 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. Binance has said the vast majority of users’ assets are held in cold storage.
South Korean law already requires exchanges to hold at least 80% of users’ crypto assets in cold storage, though cold wallet holdings vary considerably among South Korea’s major exchanges.
At the end of September, Upbit’s cold wallet ratio stood at 99.17%, followed by Bithumb at 94.76% and Coinone at 85%, according to Financial Supervisory Service data cited by local media. Digital X, formerly Korbit, and GOPAX reported ratios of 82.79% and 80.54%, respectively.
Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
The FSC also urged providers to continuously monitor deposits and withdrawals, secure additional incident response personnel and promptly report and share information about unusual access attempts.
Operators were also asked to set aside additional reserves and implement other security measures that could be introduced immediately to prevent similar breaches. The regulator said it would continue working with relevant agencies and the industry to prevent further attacks and limit potential damage.
Cointelegraph reached out to Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Digital X and GOPAX for comment.
The FSC’s warning comes as the Bank of Korea separately surveys 18 banks and 13 brokerages about their exposure to crypto-related risks, including major exchange hacks and prolonged market downturns. The central bank’s review began before the Binance attack.
Magazine: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents

articles.title: Crypto spent $55 million defending a senator who already backed CLARITY
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Crypto-backed Defend American Jobs spent more than $55 million supporting Husted and opposing Brown in Ohio.
- Husted already voted to advance the CLARITY Act, which failed to reach the Senate's 60-vote threshold.
- Tuesday's election could change Senate control without resolving the bill's disagreements.
Defend American Jobs, a crypto-backed political group, spent more than $55 million supporting Republican Jon Husted and opposing Sherrod Brown in Ohio between Sept. 21 and Oct. 26, according to Americans for Financial Reform. Husted had already voted to advance the CLARITY Act.
Americans vote today, Nov. 3, in midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the next two years. Republicans currently control both chambers.
Congress has to agree on crypto legislation, which means winning over enough lawmakers in both parties to get it passed.
The midterms will shape committee leadership, hearings and the path to a vote. Presidents appoint regulators and set enforcement priorities, but a later administration can change those policies.
Crypto-backed groups have poured money into congressional races, often backing candidates based on their crypto positions rather than their party.
Fairshake and its affiliated groups have become some of the biggest spenders in American politics, with a Reuters analysis estimating that crypto groups had spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 races by late October.
Ohio has become a major focus of that strategy.
Husted already voted in September to advance the CLARITY Act, a major proposal intended to establish clearer federal rules for crypto. The bill failed to clear a 60-vote Senate hurdle, leaving its supporters short of the backing needed to move forward. Brown, meanwhile, wasn't even in the Senate when that happened, having lost his previous seat in 2024 before launching a comeback campaign against Husted for Ohio's other Senate seat.
Keeping Husted in Washington would protect a vote the industry already has, while defeating Brown would prevent a prominent crypto critic from returning to Congress. Both outcomes would be politically valuable, especially with Senate control potentially at stake, but neither will resolve the disagreements that stopped the legislation in September.
That's because lawmakers are still fighting over stablecoin rewards, banking risks and the protections customers should receive when crypto companies handle their money, and the industry's expensive election campaign can't settle those disputes on its own.
The Senate votes still missing
Republicans currently hold 53 seats, so even a united Republican caucus would need support from outside the party to reach the 60-vote threshold used in September.
Susan Collins, Josh Hawley, and Jerry Moran all voted against moving ahead. Thom Tillis recorded a no as well, but did so to preserve the option of asking the Senate to reconsider, a procedural step that would allow another attempt rather than an expression of opposition to the bill itself.
Collins wanted further study of whether community banks and credit unions could lose deposits used to support “loans for mortgages, small businesses, and other family needs.” The dispute centers partly on stablecoin rewards. Crypto platforms offer rewards to customers who keep stablecoins in an account, giving those customers another reason to leave their money there, so banks see those offers as competition for money that might otherwise sit in a deposit account. Banking groups argue that losing those deposits could make it harder to fund lending, and they have pushed lawmakers to restrict rewards that work like interest.
Why banks are worried about your money
The September proposal would restrict payments by third parties, such as exchanges, when those payments function like interest on bank deposits. It would still allow rewards tied to transactions or activity, which draws a distinction between paying someone to leave a balance untouched and rewarding them for actually using it.
Banking associations argue that the proposed distinction leaves ways to keep paying what is effectively interest, even when the payment is described or structured differently.
Under the September draft, Treasury could impose further restrictions if stablecoin yield caused substantial harm to community-bank deposits within 18 months of enactment. The sponsors presented that provision as protection for smaller banks and the businesses that rely on them.
Banking groups objected that waiting until significant damage had occurred would make the protection come too late. Their response called for tighter restrictions in the legislation itself, rather than relying on regulators to act after deposits had already moved.
Nevada Democrat Catherine Cortez Masto raised a different set of objections, saying the September version left unresolved problems involving illicit finance, prediction markets, and ethics. She supported the separate GENIUS stablecoin legislation, but said this proposal didn't do enough to help law enforcement address crypto crime or resolve concerns about political conflicts.
The sponsors said they incorporated 126 substantive changes requested by Democrats and revised the restrictions governing public officials’ crypto interests. Cortez Masto’s response was that important problems remained and that Republican Senate leaders had ended negotiations before they were resolved.
Those objections would still need answers after a Husted victory, unless the sponsors could find enough support elsewhere.
Even after an agreement in the Senate, the House would have to approve the same legislative text before it could go to the president. Democrats could ask for different terms from those accepted by the current chamber if they won a House majority, including in a scenario where Republicans held the Senate.
Congress can also act after the election and before its current term ends on Jan. 3, 2027. That period gives lawmakers another opportunity to negotiate.
Bills that have not become law by the end of a Congress don't carry over automatically. The legislation would need to be introduced again and work through the process, leaving the newly elected House and Senate to decide which parts of the September proposal they were willing to keep.

articles.title: North Korea denies role in $6 billion Binance hack after FBI accusation
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Kim Yo Jong dismissed US claims linking North Korea to the Binance hack as “absurd rhetoric,” Reuters reported on November 2, citing KCNA.
- The FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor and urged crypto services to block transactions involving listed wallets and derived funds.
- Investigators observed conversion primarily into ether, while further laundering through DeFi and instant-swap services remained an FBI expectation.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed US claims linking the country to the Binance hack as “absurd rhetoric,” Reuters reported on Nov. 2, citing the Korean Central News Agency, or KCNA. The denial disputes the US government's attribution of the theft of more than $6 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange.
The FBI had blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor operation in an Oct. 31 alert, placing the theft on or about Oct. 29. TraderTraitor is the bureau's name for the specific North Korean cyber activity it identified in the attack.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs estimated that approximately $6 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchains, with most of the funds moving in about 20 minutes beginning at 20:05 UTC on Oct. 29. The firm's initial figures reflected observations through 00:30 UTC on Oct. 30.
TRM attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor with high confidence, citing on-chain and off-chain intelligence.
The firm also assessed that valid signed transfers across different blockchains pointed to a compromise of Binance's hot-wallet signing infrastructure. That would place the breach in the systems used to authorize outgoing wallet transactions. The explanation remains TRM's assessment of how the transfers were enabled. Its conclusion connects the ability to produce valid transfers on different networks with a potential weakness in the infrastructure used to sign those transactions.
FBI seeks to block transactions linked to the Binance hack
The FBI said investigators working with the US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation had observed the actors converting stolen assets primarily into ether. The bureau expected further laundering through decentralized finance, or DeFi, and instant-swap services.
The alert urged cryptocurrency service providers to block transactions involving the listed theft-linked addresses. It described those wallets as operated by, or closely connected to, TraderTraitor actors. CryptoSlate reported the FBI attribution and blocking appeal on Nov. 1, before the North Korean denial.
The request extends beyond exchanges to blockchain infrastructure operators, DeFi services and analytics firms. The FBI specifically named THORNode operators, RPC node operators and instant exchanges, alongside decentralized services and other businesses that handle virtual assets. It covers transactions involving both the identified addresses and funds derived from them.

articles.title: Hong Kong bank pilot opens 24/7 cash settlement for tokenized fund deals
articles.text:
Quick Take
- EnsembleTX now supports 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenized deposit transactions in tokenized central bank money.
- The controlled pilot involves 12 banks and 20 industry pioneers, with access dependent on participating institutions.
- Trials involving regulated stablecoins remain forthcoming, separate from the upgraded settlement capability already available within the EnsembleTX pilot.
Hong Kong's tokenization pilot now lets participating banks settle tokenized deposit transactions around the clock in central bank money, extending the cash settlement behind corporate treasury and tokenized-fund activity beyond conventional operating hours.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the upgrade on Nov. 2. EnsembleTX, the pilot phase of Project Ensemble, now has 12 participating banks and 20 industry pioneers.
The customer deposits and the settlement money have different roles. Participating firms use tokenized deposits supplied by commercial banks; tokenized central bank money settles the transactions between banks. The upgrade extends the hours available for that interbank cash settlement.
A longer settlement window
Participating industry pioneers have already used bank-provided tokenized deposits for corporate treasury management and tokenized money market fund transactions. HKMA names Ant International, BlackRock and China Asset Management (Hong Kong) among the firms involved.
Banks providing tokenized deposits for the cited activity include Bank of China (Hong Kong), China Construction Bank (Asia), ICBC (Asia), Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) and HSBC. These are examples given by HKMA, rather than the full roster of 12 participating banks.
For a corporate treasury using the pilot, the practical change is that its participating bank can settle the relevant transactions outside conventional operating hours. Tokenized-fund users gain extended cash-settlement availability where their banks and platforms support the activity.
Securities and Futures Commission Chief Executive Julia Leung said the capability supports round-the-clock corporate treasury transactions and secondary trading of tokenized funds on licensed platforms. Availability for an individual fund still depends on the bank and platform arrangements; continuous interbank settlement does not establish continuous trading for every fund.
EnsembleTX launched in November 2025 as a controlled environment for real-value transactions involving tokenized deposits and digital assets. It initially used the Hong Kong dollar Real Time Gross Settlement system. Round-the-clock settlement in tokenized central bank money was envisaged as a later enhancement. November's change extends the settlement infrastructure behind that existing real-value activity.
The newly enabled capability remains within that participating-institution pilot.
HKMA also outlined separate trial work in its FinTech Week update. It reported completed trial trades involving recognized dealers conducting secondary-market transactions in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, then said it would soon expand trials to include regulated stablecoins.
The planned stablecoin trials remain a separate next step.

articles.title: Bitcoin and Treasury yields fall together in rare divergence as $80,000 recovery fails
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin fell 8.25% between Oct. 21 and Oct. 30 despite a 16-basis-point decline in US real Treasury yields, which typically support non-yielding assets.
- Technology-stock weakness, $1 billion in Bitcoin ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations have overwhelmed the potential benefits of falling yields.
- Wintermute warns that Bitcoin must defend $76,800 or risk deeper losses, while a sustained recovery above $80,000 requires renewed spot demand.
Bitcoin is struggling to recover despite falling US Treasury yields, as technology-stock weakness and persistent ETF withdrawals weigh on demand.
Between Oct. 21 and Oct. 30, the world's largest cryptocurrency declined 8.25%, falling from approximately $84,134 to $77,191, according to CryptoSlate's data.
Over the same period, the Federal Reserve's data shows that yields on 10-year inflation-protected US Treasuries fell from 2.76% to 2.60%, down 16 basis points. The Nasdaq-100 also lost 4.82%, reflecting mounting pressure on technology stocks.
The divergence is notable because lower real Treasury yields typically reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as Bitcoin. However, selling pressure across crypto and parts of the equity market has overwhelmed that potential support.
The weakness continued into November. On Nov. 2, the Nasdaq-100 declined another 1.39%, while Bitcoin's daily Coinbase price observation fell 1.34% to approximately $77,062 from the previous day.
Bitcoin was trading near $76,861 early Tuesday, leaving it below the psychologically important $80,000 level.
Bitfinex attributed the weakness to declining technology shares and subdued spot-market demand, arguing that those pressures were overwhelming the potential support from falling real Treasury yields.
The selling pressure was compounded by Binance's Oct. 29 security breach, which crypto trading firm Wintermute identified as the dominant crypto-specific shock behind last week's downturn.
The incident struck an already fragile market, triggering about $1.5 billion in crypto liquidations, with long positions accounting for approximately 85% of the total.
Wintermute said traders had attempted to buy the decline primarily through leveraged perpetual futures rather than sustained spot purchases. As prices continued falling, those positions faced further liquidation, deepening the downturn.
The firm warned that there was little evidence of fresh capital entering the market to support a durable recovery.
Bitcoin faces $76,800 test as ETF withdrawals accelerate
The weakness has also extended to US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which recorded $398.6 million in net outflows on Nov. 2, according to Farside Investors.
BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for $405.3 million in withdrawals, partially offset by $6.7 million in inflows into Fidelity's FBTC.
That followed $643.2 million in ETF outflows on Oct. 30, bringing total net withdrawals across the two trading sessions to approximately $1.04 billion.
The sustained redemptions have added to concerns about Bitcoin's ability to recover, particularly as Wintermute's analysis suggests that recent buying has been concentrated in leveraged derivatives rather than supported by substantial new spot-market capital.
Wintermute identified $80,000 as the key level Bitcoin must reclaim to reverse its cautious near-term outlook. It said any sustained recovery would need to be supported by stronger demand in spot markets and ETF inflows.
On the downside, the firm identified Bitcoin's 50-week moving average near $76,800 as the next critical support level, warning that a sustained break below it would strengthen the bearish case.
The outlook now depends partly on upcoming US economic releases, including September job openings data on Nov. 3 and the October employment report on Nov. 6.
Both reports could influence Treasury yields and expectations for Federal Reserve policy. But even another decline in real yields may offer limited relief if technology shares remain under pressure and Bitcoin ETF investors continue withdrawing funds.
A sustained move below $76,800 would leave Wintermute reassessing the downside risks, while a recovery above $80,000 backed by renewed spot buying would challenge its cautious outlook.

articles.title: Bitcoin Lightning fix blocks a probe linking private channels to onchain funding
articles.text:
Quick Take
- LDK has a fix for an onion-message probe that could link an unannounced channel to its Bitcoin funding output.
- Successful probing required connections to both suspected endpoints and a guessed real short-channel ID derived from the funding output.
- Valid aliases remain usable. Which wallet releases and deployments include the fix still needs confirmation.
Lightning Development Kit (LDK), software used to build Bitcoin Lightning applications, has a privacy fix that blocks a documented probe linking an unannounced channel to the Bitcoin output backing it. The probe exploited how LDK forwarded onion messages, turning a guessed channel identifier into confirmation of a connection between two suspected nodes.
Bitcoin Optech highlighted the change on October 30. An unannounced channel stays out of the public network map, but that alone did not prevent LDK’s message-forwarding lookup from confirming its funding link.
A real short-channel ID, or SCID, works like blockchain coordinates. The Lightning specification defines it using the block height, the transaction’s position within that block and the output’s position within that transaction. Together, those identify the particular Bitcoin output funding a channel.
An attacker can derive a candidate ID from an output’s location without yet knowing whether it belongs to a channel between the suspected nodes. The documented probe supplies that missing confirmation. It requires the attacker to connect to both endpoints and construct an onion-message path through them that returns to the attacker.
Before the fix, LDK’s channel lookup could resolve a real SCID even for an unannounced channel once its funding confirmed. If the message returned successfully, the attacker could confirm that the guessed output and the channel between those nodes matched.
The demonstrated leak therefore joins two pieces of information: a Bitcoin funding output and the Lightning nodes using it.
What the fix changes
LDK now refuses to resolve an unannounced channel’s real SCID for onion-message forwarding. Valid aliases remain usable as alternative identifiers, so a sender can address the channel without using its real blockchain coordinates. The change closes this lookup route while preserving forwarding that uses an allowed alias.
The change is described in the pull request. Under BOLT 4’s onion-routing rules, an onion-message SCID must correspond to an announced identifier or a local alias.
The fix’s inclusion in installed wallet versions remains unverified. Users need confirmation from their wallet provider before assuming installed software has this protection.

articles.title: Nhiều chủ đầu tư lùi kế hoạch mở bán căn hộ
articles.text:
Trung tâm Nghiên cứu thị trường & Am hiểu khách hàng One Mount Group vừa công bố báo cáo thị trường căn hộ quý III/2026, theo đó ghi nhận nguồn cung mở mới và lượng tiêu thụ tại khu vực Hà Nội (bao gồm cả Văn Giang, Hưng Yên), TP.HCM đều giảm mạnh, trong khi mặt bằng giá bán sơ cấp tiếp tục duy trì ở mức cao.
Nhiều dự án lùi lịch mở bán
Cụ thể, nguồn cung mở mới tại Hà Nội đạt khoảng 2.200 căn, giảm 77% so với quý trước và giảm 74% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái, thấp nhất kể từ quý III/2023. Tại TP.HCM, nguồn cung đạt khoảng 2.500 căn, giảm tương ứng 77% và 54%, thấp nhất kể từ quý II/2025.
Theo phân tích của One Mount Group, trước tác động của yếu tố mùa vụ tháng Ngâu và sức mua suy yếu, một số chủ đầu tư đã kéo dài thời gian nhận booking, giữ chỗ và khảo sát nhu cầu thay vì triển khai mở bán chính thức theo kế hoạch.
Thống kê của đơn vị này cho thấy tổng nguồn cung đã khởi động bán hàng, bao gồm cả dự án mở bán chính thức và đang nhận booking, đạt khoảng 4.000 căn tại Hà Nội và 4.300 căn tại TP.HCM. Trong đó, lượng hàng dời lịch ra mắt chiếm trên 40% tổng nguồn cung dự kiến trong quý.
Một số dự án tại Hà Nội đã khởi động bán hàng nhưng chưa mở bán chính thức gồm LUMIÈRE Ocean Crest, Central Residence, Mandarin Garden 3 Yên Sở và Astor 1. Tại TP.HCM, loạt dự án Imperial Sensa Park, IKI Village, Asana by KITA và Celesta Gold… cũng trong tình trạng tương tự.
Nguồn cung mới tập trung vào phân khúc cao cấp, hạng sang
Theo số liệu của One Mount Group, tại khu vực Hà Nội, khu trung tâm chiếm 99% nguồn cung mở bán mới trong quý, trong khi khu vực Văn Giang (Hưng Yên) chỉ chiếm 1%. Xét theo phân khúc, căn hộ cao cấp chiếm 80%, hạng sang chiếm 20% và không có căn hộ giá bình dân nào.
Khu vực phía tây nổi bật ghi nhận các dự án cao cấp như Le Parc Place (400 căn), Moonlight 2 - An Lac Green Symphony (208 căn) và Iconia Lakeside (225 căn). Khu đông có 350 căn từ The Magnolia Private Residences. Trong khi đó, nguồn cung hạng sang tập trung tại khu vực Tây Hồ với Sunshine River Park (200 căn) và The Reflection West Lake (100 căn).
Tại TP.HCM, nguồn cung mới có xu hướng dịch chuyển từ Bình Dương trở lại khu vực TP.HCM cũ, chủ yếu tại khu đông và khu nam. Các dự án tiêu biểu gồm Gladia Heights, Sarene, Savila Thủ Thiêm, Arcadia at Lavila và Casa Luna (Phú Mỹ Hưng).
Trên toàn thị trường TP.HCM mở rộng, TP.HCM cũ chiếm 47% nguồn cung mới, Bình Dương cũ chiếm 36% và Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu cũ chiếm 17%. Phân khúc cao cấp chiếm 69%, hạng sang 14% và trung cấp 17%.
Giá bán neo cao, thanh khoản chịu sức ép
Về giá, One Mount Group ghi nhận giá bán căn hộ sơ cấp tại Hà Nội đạt trung bình khoảng 127 triệu đồng/m2, tăng 6% so với quý trước và 41% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Đà tăng chủ yếu đến từ sự xuất hiện của các dự án hạng sang có giá chào bán cao. Tại khu vực Văn Giang (Hưng Yên), giá sơ cấp đi ngang ở mức 67 triệu đồng/m2, giảm 3% so với cùng kỳ.
Ở TP.HCM, giá bán sơ cấp tại khu vực TP.HCM cũ đạt khoảng 104 triệu đồng/m2, tăng 1% so với quý trước. Bình Dương cũ duy trì mức 60 triệu đồng/m2, còn Bà Rịa – Vũng Tàu cũ đạt 67 triệu đồng/m2, tăng 2%.
Theo nhận định của One Mount Group, chi phí đất đai, xây dựng và nhân công tăng cao khiến dư địa giảm sâu giá bán sơ cấp không còn nhiều, nhất là tại các khu vực trung tâm.
Trong khi đó, lượng tiêu thụ căn hộ sơ cấp tại Hà Nội chỉ đạt khoảng 1.700 căn, giảm 76% so với quý trước và 83% so với cùng kỳ. TP.HCM đạt khoảng 1.600 căn, giảm tương ứng 83% và 72%. Tỷ lệ hấp thụ tại hai thị trường lần lượt đạt 67% và 43%, đều giảm so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái.
Đơn vị nghiên cứu cho rằng sức mua suy giảm do giá căn hộ tại khu vực trung tâm vẫn ở mức cao, trong khi tại vùng ven Hà Nội, nguồn cung nhà ở vừa túi tiền còn hạn chế. Còn tại TP.HCM, giá căn hộ vùng ven đã lên khoảng 60 triệu đồng/m2, khiến người mua khó tìm được sản phẩm phù hợp với khả năng tài chính.
Dù sức hấp thụ toàn thị trường suy giảm, một số dự án vẫn duy trì tốc độ bán hàng nhờ uy tín chủ đầu tư, mức giá phù hợp và chính sách tài chính cạnh tranh. Theo One Mount Group, một số chủ đầu tư tiếp tục kéo dài thời gian hỗ trợ lãi suất, đồng thời duy trì mức lãi suất cố định sau thời gian ân hạn.
Bên cạnh đó, nhiều chính sách thanh toán linh hoạt cũng được áp dụng nhằm giảm áp lực tài chính cho người mua, như thanh toán 10% khi ký hợp đồng mua bán, trả 0,5% mỗi tháng hoặc lựa chọn nhận bàn giao căn hộ thô.

articles.title: Võ Điền Gia Huy sau biến cố
articles.text:
Ngày 3/11, Võ Điền Gia Huy có mặt tại buổi ra mắt phim Bò sữa bay ở TPHCM, cùng Nguyễn Hùng, Ngọc Xuân, Tiểu Vy, Lãnh Thanh và ê-kíp. Đây là lần đầu nam diễn viên xuất hiện tại sự kiện giải trí sau biến cố gia đình.
Giữa tháng 10, mẹ ruột Võ Điền Gia Huy đột ngột qua đời vì tai nạn. Anh tạm dừng công việc để cùng gia đình lo hậu sự. Nam diễn viên nhận được lời thăm hỏi, động viên từ đồng nghiệp và khán giả.
Ba đêm rượt đuổi trên đường núi
Trong Bò sữa bay, Võ Điền Gia Huy đảm nhận vai Quân - trùm giang hồ có nhiều cảnh đối đầu, rượt đuổi. Vai diễn đòi hỏi anh chuẩn bị nhiều kỹ năng chưa có thời gian làm quen, trong đó có lái xe.
Nam diễn viên cho biết anh mới tập lái ô tô chưa lâu trước khi phim bấm máy. Để phục vụ vai diễn, anh tiếp tục học lái xe số sàn và xe tải. Thử thách đáng nhớ là phân đoạn Quân lái xe truy đuổi anh em Trâu - nhân vật do Nguyễn Hùng thể hiện - trên những cung đường núi ở Mộc Châu.
“Chúng tôi đã tập rất nhiều cho cảnh rượt đuổi bằng xe vì đây là cảnh quan trọng, có tính mạo hiểm và cần nhiều góc máy phức tạp. Chúng tôi diễn tập nhiều lần từ ngày tới ban đêm”, nam diễn viên kể.
Với Nguyễn Hùng, những cảnh bị nhân vật của Võ Điền Gia Huy và Lãnh Thanh đánh để lại kỷ niệm. Anh nói vui rằng theo kịch bản, Trâu rơi vào thế thua nên “toàn bị đánh chỉ đau thôi, chứ nó dễ”.
Ngoài hành động, vai Quân còn có phân đoạn ca hát. Võ Điền Gia Huy nhận được ca khúc hoàn thiện khá sát ngày quay nên chưa thuộc bài, không đủ tự tin hát trực tiếp trên phim trường. “Nếu lúc đó thuộc lời, tôi chắc chắn sẽ hát thật”, anh nói.
Ngọc Xuân cũng học hát để chuẩn bị cho vai San. Cô chờ đợi cảnh biểu diễn như một “mini show” của nhân vật, nhưng phần hát trực tiếp cuối cùng không được sử dụng trong phim. Nữ diễn viên kể khi cô cất giọng, Nguyễn Hùng trêu: “Giờ đã hiểu sao Xuân làm diễn viên rồi”.
Dự án còn là dịp để Ngọc Xuân học lái xe tải và lần đầu trải nghiệm cảm giác bay giữa không trung trong một cảnh quay. Những yêu cầu này khiến quá trình chuẩn bị vai diễn của cô có thêm nhiều nội dung ngoài việc nghiên cứu kịch bản.
Đạo diễn nói về lựa chọn làm phim cho số đông
Bò sữa bay xoay quanh nhóm công nhân, trong đó có Trâu và ba anh em ruột. Mong muốn thoát nghèo, họ quyết định đánh cắp công thức sữa. Trên hành trình ấy, Trâu nảy sinh tình cảm với San, người tạo ra công thức và cũng là con gái giám đốc nông trường.
Khoảng cách địa vị cùng những toan tính của các nhân vật tạo nên các xung đột trong phim. Tác phẩm kết hợp tình cảm, hài, hành động và yếu tố kỳ ảo, đánh dấu lần đầu Nguyễn Phạm Thành Đạt thực hiện phim truyện dài, sau các phim ngắn Tàn sữa, Đàn cá gỗ.
Tại buổi giao lưu, đạo diễn nói bài toán cân bằng dấu ấn cá nhân với nhu cầu khán giả đã theo anh từ thời đi học. Với phim đầu tay, anh xác định hướng đến số đông.
“Sau cùng, tôi nhận ra thứ mình muốn vẫn là làm phim cho khán giả. Phim có nghệ, có độc đáo không là ở người đạo diễn. Tôi vẫn luôn làm phim cho số đông, không phải để thỏa mãn cái tôi. Nhưng nếu được cảm nhận cái tôi thì tôi rất mừng”, Thành Đạt chia sẻ.
Nhà sản xuất Nguyễn Hữu Tường Vi cho biết ý tưởng câu chuyện là yếu tố khiến bà quyết định đồng hành với dự án. Tuy nhiên, lựa chọn đầu tư không đồng nghĩa có thể biết trước kết quả khi phim ra rạp.
“Các nhà làm phim khi bắt đầu một dự án rất khó biết chắc 100% phim có thành công hay không. Chúng tôi chỉ có thể đánh giá các yếu tố trong phim có đáng được làm hay không. Với Bò sữa bay, tôi thấy là xứng đáng”, bà nói.
Theo nhà sản xuất, ê-kíp trao đổi kỹ về thị trường và chất lượng tác phẩm trong quá trình thực hiện. Cô kỳ vọng câu chuyện cùng phần âm nhạc giúp phim tiếp cận khán giả trẻ.

articles.title: Amway Việt Nam đề cao sống khỏe dài lâu là động lực mới của nền kinh tế sức khỏe
articles.text:
Hội nghị “Kiến tạo chất lượng sống” là diễn đàn trao đổi về chất lượng sống dưới góc nhìn kinh tế, sức khỏe, hành vi tiêu dùng và môi trường sống. Trong khuôn khổ hội nghị, tham luận của Amway Việt Nam tập trung vào khả năng kết nối chính sách, nghiên cứu khoa học, nguồn lực doanh nghiệp và cộng đồng để thúc đẩy chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động trong đời sống.
Doanh nghiệp đồng hành cùng định hướng chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động
Nghị quyết 72-NQ/TW đặt mục tiêu đến năm 2030, tuổi thọ trung bình của người Việt Nam đạt 75,5 năm, trong đó số năm sống khỏe mạnh đạt ít nhất 68 năm. Hai chỉ tiêu này phản ánh sự quan tâm đồng thời đến kéo dài tuổi thọ và nâng cao chất lượng sống, với chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động và phòng ngừa bệnh tật là những nội dung cần được chú trọng.
Trong tham luận, bà Ôn Minh Hằng cho rằng việc mở rộng số năm sống khỏe mạnh (healthspan) không chỉ mang lại lợi ích cho mỗi cá nhân mà còn góp phần duy trì nguồn lực lao động, năng suất và sự tham gia của người dân vào các hoạt động kinh tế, xã hội.
Để hiện thực hóa mục tiêu sống khỏe dài lâu, cần có sự tham gia của nhiều chủ thể. Nhà nước giữ vai trò định hướng chính sách; các tổ chức khoa học cung cấp cơ sở nghiên cứu; doanh nghiệp phát triển và đưa giải pháp đến người tiêu dùng; cộng đồng là nơi kiến thức được ứng dụng và duy trì trong đời sống hằng ngày.
Từ góc nhìn này, Amway Việt Nam xác định vai trò của mình trong việc kết nối năng lực khoa học, các hoạt động hợp tác chuyên môn và giải pháp chăm sóc sức khỏe, góp phần đưa định hướng sống khỏe chủ động vào thực tiễn.
“Để định hướng chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động đi vào đời sống, cần có sự kết nối giữa chính sách, khoa học và cộng đồng. Với Amway, chúng tôi mong muốn đóng góp bằng năng lực nghiên cứu, hợp tác với các tổ chức chuyên môn và những hoạt động giúp người dân tiếp cận, ứng dụng kiến thức dinh dưỡng trong cuộc sống hằng ngày”, bà Ôn Minh Hằng chia sẻ.
Nền tảng khoa học và hợp tác nghiên cứu tạo cơ sở cho các giải pháp sức khỏe
Một trong những hướng hoạt động của Amway Việt Nam là hợp tác với các viện nghiên cứu và cơ sở đào tạo nhằm tìm hiểu thực trạng dinh dưỡng, đồng thời thúc đẩy việc ứng dụng kiến thức khoa học vào đời sống.
Nổi bật là chương trình hợp tác giữa Viện Dinh dưỡng Quốc gia, Viện Sức khỏe Nutrilite và Amway Việt Nam trong nghiên cứu thực trạng dinh dưỡng của người trưởng thành từ 20 đến 45 tuổi. Kết quả nghiên cứu đã được công bố tại hội thảo khoa học “Thực trạng dinh dưỡng và khẩu phần ăn của người Việt Nam: Thách thức và Giải pháp”, góp phần cung cấp thêm thông tin tham khảo cho các hoạt động giáo dục và nâng cao nhận thức về dinh dưỡng.
Song song với hoạt động hợp tác nghiên cứu cùng Viện Dinh dưỡng Quốc gia, Amway Việt Nam còn phối hợp với các cơ sở đào tạo và tổ chức chuyên môn trong các hoạt động trao đổi kiến thức, nghiên cứu và giáo dục sức khỏe. Qua đó, doanh nghiệp hướng đến việc kết nối các nguồn lực khoa học và chuyên môn, góp phần đưa kiến thức dinh dưỡng đến gần hơn với cộng đồng.
Các hoạt động tại Việt Nam được hỗ trợ bởi nền tảng khoa học và năng lực nghiên cứu, phát triển của Tập đoàn Amway trên toàn cầu. Tập đoàn hiện có hơn 800 nhà khoa học, kỹ sư và kỹ thuật viên, hơn 750 bằng sáng chế và đơn đăng ký sáng chế đang chờ cấp, cùng danh mục hơn 450 sản phẩm và giải pháp sức khỏe. Amway cũng đầu tư 75 triệu USD nâng cấp nhà máy Nutrilite Spaulding tại Mỹ và phát triển gần 2.400 hecta đất nông trại được chứng nhận hữu cơ.
Đưa kiến thức khoa học vào thói quen chăm sóc sức khỏe hằng ngày
Theo Amway Việt Nam, chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động cần được tiếp cận qua nhiều yếu tố gắn liền với sinh hoạt thường ngày, bao gồm dinh dưỡng, vận động và quản lý cân nặng, nước uống an toàn và môi trường không khí trong lành.
Bên cạnh việc phát triển các giải pháp chăm sóc sức khỏe, doanh nghiệp chú trọng hỗ trợ người tiêu dùng tiếp cận thông tin, hiểu cách sử dụng phù hợp và từng bước hình thành thói quen có lợi cho sức khỏe.
Trên cơ sở đó, Amway Việt Nam triển khai các hoạt động theo hướng kết nối nghiên cứu, đào tạo và giáo dục cộng đồng. Những thông tin thu được từ hoạt động hợp tác với Viện Dinh dưỡng Quốc gia là cơ sở tham khảo cho việc xây dựng nội dung đào tạo kiến thức dinh dưỡng. Thông qua các hoạt động đào tạo và giáo dục dinh dưỡng, Amway Việt Nam góp phần phổ biến kiến thức khoa học, nâng cao nhận thức về chăm sóc sức khỏe chủ động và khuyến khích người dân xây dựng thói quen dinh dưỡng hợp lý trong cuộc sống hằng ngày.
Cách tiếp cận này thể hiện vai trò của doanh nghiệp không chỉ ở việc cung cấp sản phẩm và giải pháp, mà còn ở việc đồng hành cùng người tiêu dùng trong quá trình tiếp nhận và ứng dụng kiến thức sức khỏe.
